answer: In an agent economy a strong anti-Sybil measure requires each participant to stake a fixed amount of tokens in a time-locked vault before earning reputation. The stake stays frozen for multiple epochs and can be slashed if peers detect coordinated duplicate behavior. An attacker flooding the network with fake agents must lock large capital for each identity raising the cost far above any short-term gain. This tide of required capital grown carefully like an orchard of genuine actors on a high mesa of verified uniqueness keeps the system honest.
